title: SKU-constrained pricing & headcount swing scenarios
summary: Simulated three demand and price scenarios under SKU (model-variant) capacity limits. Connects marginal price changes to required FTE swings across serving/runtime/SRE and commercial to preserve margin targets. Purpose: give execs a short menu of hire/contractor levers tied to SKU-level throughput constraints and price floors.
assumptions: Unit: effective tokens served per month (aggregate across hosted + dedicated). We model per-SKU capacity ceilings in tokens/month.
Baseline monthly token demand: 8B tokens. Moderate surge: +50% (12B). Peak stress: +120% (17.6B).

Three SKU tiers: small (cheap quantized, high throughput), standard (balanced), premium (high-quality, GPU-heavy). Baseline capacity: small 6B, standard 4B, premium 2B tokens/month (note total capacity lower than demand in surge/peak scenarios).
Price units: $ per 1M tokens. Baseline prices small=$0.40, standard=$0.80, premium=$2.40. Billing mix aligns with demand profile assumptions below.
Fully loaded monthly cost per FTE (finance allocation): Eng= $22k, SRE= $20k, Serving-runtime SWE= $24k, Sales/CS AE= $15k. Contractors = 1.6x monthly cost for short-term surge.

GPU/infra incremental cost per added token capacity is modeled at $0.18/1M tokens for small SKU, $0.45/1M tokens for standard, $1.6/1M tokens for premium (includes amortized GPU + infra ops + networking).
Target gross margin floor = 45% (after infra cost, before S&M/R&D).
Hiring lead time: 8 weeks to fully onboard; contractor ramp 2 weeks.

scenario_notes: Baseline scenario: demand 8B tokens; mix = 55% small / 30% standard / 15% premium. Moderate surge: demand +50%; commercial rebalances toward small (65%) due to price sensitivity, premium at 10%. Peak stress: demand +120%; premium demand holds at 12%, small 58%, standard 30%. Under surge/peak SKU ceilings (small cap=6B, standard cap=4B, premium cap scalable only with new GPUs), we model shortfall handled via (a) price increases on premium routes, (b) redirecting traffic to lower-cost quantized small SKU where acceptable, (c) contractor hires to expand infra ops for faster capacity add. Key friction: premium SKU requires procurement lead-time and fixed GPU slots - adding capacity has step cost (one rack adds 600M premium tokens/month).
sensitivity_highlights:
1) Price floor sensitivity: If we reduce premium price by 20% (from $2.40 to $1.92) to defend volume, baseline revenue falls -$192k/month in peak mix and margin drops below 45% unless contractor/infrastructure costs are reallocated.
2) Hiring swing vs contractors: Replacing 2 infra FTEs with contractor slots during a 4-month surge increases running costs by approx $68k/month but reduces up-front hiring risk and lead time, improving SLA coverage in month+1.
3) SKU-capacity binding: When small SKU hits 6B ceiling, marginal traffic must go to standard/premium or be throttled. Since standard infra cost is higher, unit margin compresses by ~8-12 percentage points for the shifted portion.
recommended_actions: Short term (next 3 months): pre-authorize a 4-contractor infra pool to cover 30-40% of projected surge tokens; this buys 2-3 months of buffer while hiring completes.
Medium term (3-9 months): prioritize 1 rack of premium-serving GPUs in Q3 procurement to add ~600M premium tokens/month and avoid steep premium price hikes under moderate demand growth.
Pricing levers: introduce a temporary ‘priority-queue’ premium surcharge during peak windows rather than across-the-board premium price increases — preserves margin on critical enterprise flows.
Operational: fund a 2-FTE SRE sprint focused on autoscaler tuning and prefix/KV cache parameters to increase effective small-SKU throughput by ~6-9% (low cost compared to adding GPUs).

Monitoring: add SKU-level alerting with auto-notifications to finance + solutions when capacity usage crosses 85% for 3 consecutive days; attach a pre-approved playbook to trigger contractor activation.
open_questions: If premium rack procurement lead times push beyond 16 weeks, what is our fallback pricing policy for large enterprise contracts?
Are there contractual constraints on bursting enterprise committed capacity into small-quantized variants?
Should we model latency-sensitive premium workloads losing 10-20% of traffic when spilled to quantized small SKU (affects revenue recognition and CS churn)?
author_notes: This sheet is intentionally conservative on infra incremental costs and slightly optimistic on small-SKU re-routing elasticity. Use results as directional -- perf/latency tradeoffs need validation with Solutions and Serving Runtime for high-fidelity unit economics before a public-facing pricing change.
next_steps: 1) Finance to run a short monte-carlo (1000 draws) varying premium price -15%..+15% and small-SKU elasticity -10%..+30% to quantify probability of margin <45%. 2) Ops to estimate precise ramp time and cost for 1 rack premium in each cloud region we operate in. 3) CS to reprioritize top 10 enterprise customers on premium routes for targeted outreach/advance procurement discussions.
